caption: Figure 1. Illustration of our framework. (a) FPN backbone. (b) Bottom-up path augmentation. (c) Adaptive feature pooling. (d) Box branch. (e) Fully-connected fusion. Note that we omit channel dimension of feature maps in (a) and (b) for brevity.
description:
## Figure Description
This figure illustrates the framework of the Path Aggregation Network for Instance Segmentation. It consists of five panels labeled (a) to (e), each depicting a different component of the network.

- Panel (a) shows the FPN (Feature Pyramid Network) backbone, which processes input images to produce feature maps labeled P2 to P5.
- Panel (b) demonstrates the bottom-up path augmentation, where additional paths are created from the feature maps.
- Panel (c) illustrates the adaptive feature pooling, which combines features from different levels.
- Panel (d) shows the box branch, which predicts bounding boxes for detected objects.
- Panel (e) depicts the fully-connected fusion, where features are combined to produce the final output, including class labels, bounding boxes, and masks.

- Feature Pyramid Network (FPN)
- Bottom-up Path Augmentation
- Adaptive Feature Pooling

caption: Figure 4. Mask prediction branch with fully-connected fusion.
description:
Description: The figure illustrates a neural network architecture for mask prediction in instance segmentation. It shows a sequence of convolutional layers (conv1 to conv4) followed by a deconvolution layer (deconv). The output of the deconvolution layer is reshaped and then passed through two fully connected layers (conv4_fc and conv5_fc). The final output is a mask, which is the result of element-wise multiplication with a mask.

caption: Figure 6. Illustration of adaptive feature pooling on box branch.
description:
This figure illustrates the adaptive feature pooling process on the box branch of the Path Aggregation Network for instance segmentation. It shows how features from different regions of interest (ROIs) are pooled and processed through fully connected layers (fc1 and fc2) to predict the class and bounding box of an object. The process starts with ROIAlign, which extracts features from the input feature map. These features are then passed through fc1 and fc2 layers, with the final output being the class and box predictions.
